anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Query Plan Selection Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : User-written statements or transaction flows request more data, rows, or time than the business logic really needs.
Query Plan Selection Anomaly : The optimizer chooses a markedly sub-optimal execution plan even though statistics are reasonably accurate.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Network, listener, or connection-slot resources cannot keep up with the request or result-set volume, throttling traffic between client and server.

Composite definition: The system simultaneously suffers from excessive or ill-formed workload demands, poor optimizer decisions that amplify data access costs, and constrained network/connection resources. The net effect is an over-sized and poorly executed workload whose results are pushed through a saturated transport layer, producing a multi-layer performance collapse.

Combined anomalous phenomena: 1) Statements that already scan or join far more rows than necessary are executed with plans that choose full table scans, non-sargable predicates, or mismatched join algorithms, causing CPU, I/O, and memory spikes. 2) Result sets are larger and take longer to transmit, so back-end sessions accumulate client-read/client-write waits while front-end threads block on socket or connection pool exhaustion. 3) Slow or failed connection attempts, rising retransmission counts, and retry storms coincide with volatile plan caches and frequent plan flips. 4) Application timeouts, lock escalations, and long-tail latencies appear indistinguishable from pure network or pure database issues because symptoms propagate across layers.

Causal chain analysis: Mis-scoped SQL inflates the data volume the engine must process. When the optimizer then selects an unfavorable plan, that data volume multiplies, enlarging intermediate and final result sets. The swollen result streams clog limited network bandwidth and consume connection slots for extended periods, which in turn slow new session establishment and prolong transaction lifetimes. Longer execution and transport times increase the chance of parameter-value shifts or cache invalidations that trigger further poor plan selections, while client-side retries increase the statement rate and intensify both the planning bottleneck and network congestion. This feedback loop magnifies resource contention across compute, storage, and network layers, yielding a performance degradation far worse than any single anomaly alone.

entry.official_definition: Specifies the amount of time after which a TCP keepalive message that has not been acknowledged by the client should be retransmitted.
entry.trigger_condition: A TCP keepalive probe is not acknowledged for tcp_keepalives_interval on systems supporting TCP_KEEPINTVL or an equivalent socket option.
entry.workload_impact: Controls retry timing for keepalive probes used to detect unresponsive client connections.
entry.default_behavior: Default value is 0, selecting the operating system default.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
